answer:
Based on the analysis performed, here are the results:

## Incident Counts and Rates per Zone

I spatially joined the 256 incidents to the 9 zones (251 matched a zone; 5 fell outside all zones) and combined the counts with each zone's population.

| Zone | Population | Incidents | Rate per 1,000 |
|------|-----------:|----------:|---------------:|
| Z1 | 5,200 | 41 | 7.88 |
| **Z2** | **830** | **19** | **22.89** |
| Z3 | 4,100 | 22 | 5.37 |
| Z4 | 2,600 | 18 | 6.92 |
| Z5 | 7,400 | 66 | 8.92 |
| Z6 | 3,900 | 25 | 6.41 |
| Z7 | 1,500 | 9 | 6.00 |
| Z8 | 6,100 | 37 | 6.07 |
| Z9 | 2,800 | 14 | 5.00 |

## Answer

**Zone Z2 has the highest rate at 22.89 incidents per 1,000 residents.**

This is driven by its small population (830 residents) relative to its 19 incidents — more than 2.5× the next-highest zone (Z5 at 8.92). Note that Z5 has the most incidents in absolute terms (66), but its much larger population (7,400) brings its rate down.
